content: The studies referenced explore various telehealth interventions and their impacts on healthcare delivery. 1. Hunkeler et al. (2000): This study evaluated the effectiveness of nurse-led telehealth care and peer support in enhancing the treatment of depression within primary care settings. The intervention aimed to improve patient outcomes by integrating telecommunication methods and peer support into standard care practices. 2. Kooy et al. (2015): This research investigated the impact of a pharmacist-led telephone counseling intervention (TelCIP) on medication adherence. The study, conducted as a cluster randomized trial, demonstrated that telephone-based counseling could positively influence patients' adherence to prescribed medications. 3. Kooy et al. (2014): This study outlined the protocol for a cluster randomized controlled trial examining the effects of pharmacist-led telephone counseling on medication adherence, patient beliefs, and satisfaction with information provided to patients initiating treatment. The intervention aimed to address gaps in patient education and support. 4. Kooy et al. (2015): This trial assessed patients' overall satisfaction with pharmacist-led telephone counseling and its effects on their satisfaction with medication-related information and beliefs. The results highlighted the potential of telephonic interventions to enhance patient satisfaction and trust in their treatment plans. 5. Looman et al. (2015): This study focused on a telehealth care coordination model led by advanced practice registered nurses to address the needs of children with medical complexity. The intervention aimed to improve care coordination and outcomes for this vulnerable population. 6. Looman et al. (2015): This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of a telehealth care coordination intervention on caregivers' perceptions of healthcare for children with medical complexity. The findings suggested that telehealth could positively influence caregivers' experiences and satisfaction with care. 7. McKissick et al. (2017): This study examined the impact of telehealth and care coordination on the frequency and type of clinical visits for children with medical complexity. The intervention aimed to optimize healthcare utilization and reduce unnecessary visits. 8. McCrossan et al. (2012): This randomized trial investigated a remote home support program for infants with major congenital heart disease. The program utilized telehealth to provide continuous monitoring and support, aiming to improve outcomes and reduce hospitalizations. 9. Zillich et al. (2014): This pragmatic randomized controlled trial assessed the effectiveness of telephonic medication therapy management in reducing hospitalizations among home health patients. The intervention targeted improved medication management and adherence. 10. Smith et al. (2015): This randomized controlled trial in Cambodia evaluated the effect of a mobile phone-based intervention on post-abortion contraception use. The study demonstrated the potential of mobile health technologies to improve reproductive health outcomes. 11. Westra and Niessen (2015): This study explored the implementation of real-time video consultations in plastic surgery. The intervention aimed to enhance patient-provider communication and streamline preoperative and postoperative care. 12. Bergmo et al. (2005): This research examined whether electronic communication between patients and providers could reduce the need for office visits and telephone consultations in primary care. The study highlighted the potential of digital communication to improve efficiency in healthcare delivery. 13. Bikmoradi et al. (2016): This quasi-experimental study in Iran investigated the impact of tele-nursing on adherence to treatment plans among patients discharged after coronary artery bypass graft surgery. The intervention aimed to improve post-discharge care and adherence. 14. Freeman et al. (2013): This study evaluated the use of Skype for behavioral healthcare in adolescents with poorly controlled diabetes. The research focused on whether the therapeutic alliance between patients and providers remained intact in a virtual setting. 15. Galbreath et al. (2004): This randomized trial assessed the impact of disease management programs on quality of life in patients with congestive heart failure. The study found limited improvements in quality of life despite the intervention. 16. Reynolds et al. (2008): This multisite randomized controlled trial examined the use of telephone support to improve adherence to antiretroviral therapy. The intervention targeted better medication adherence among patients with HIV. 17. Cochrane Review (2017): This systematic review assessed the effects of mobile-based telemedicine for provider-to-provider communication and client management. The review included 12 studies and highlighted the potential of telemedicine to improve healthcare delivery, particularly in settings with limited resources. These studies collectively underscore the growing role of telehealth and telemedicine in enhancing healthcare delivery, improving patient outcomes, and addressing gaps in access to care.
